newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GREMIO SHOW UGLY SIDE ON SOUR LIBERTADORES NIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GREMIO SHOW UGLY SIDE ON SOUR LIBERTADORES NIGHT.

text.p: Brazilian champions Gremio showed their ugly side as they lost 1-0 away to Peru's Sporting Cristal on a night of general bad behaviour in the South American Libertadores Cup on Friday.

Gremio's self-styled hard man Dinho was sent off in the first half, while television cameras caught defender Catalino Rivarola elbowing an opponent in the face in an off-the-ball incident apparently not seen by the referee.
Their opponents also finished with ten men after having Marcelo Asteggiano sent off for a second bookable offence.

In Montevideo, both coaches got their marching orders in the game between Uruguayan champions Penarol and Millonarios of Colombia, who also had a midfielder Hilmer Lozano dismissed in their 2-1 defeat.

Gregorio Perez of Penarol was ordered to leave the bench for arguing in the 75th minute and his counterpart Angel Castelnoble suffered the same fate in the 85th minute, ironically after his team had just pulled a goal back.

Bolivar's Jefferson Gottardi was sent off for fighting only three minutes after coming on as a substitute as the Bolivian champions won 3-1 at home to Cerro Porteno, the champions of Paraguay, in La Paz.
Gremio were Libertadores champions in 1995 but made more enemies than friends with their ruthless style of play.
They appeared to have turned over a new leaf with a stylish 4-0 demolition of Alianza, the other Peruvian side in first round group four, on Tuesday.

But on Friday, the old Gremio appeared to have made a comeback. Dinho had already been booked for viciously kicking an opponent when he got entangled with another Sporting player in the 44th minute and was sent off.
Gremio players also wasted much time bickering with the referee, especially at halftime when the official was escorted off the pitch by police wielding riot shields.
Norberto Solano scored the winner for Sporting with a penalty in the sixth minute.
The defeat is unlikely to do Gremio much harm as only the last of the four teams in the each group will be eliminated in the first round.
Gremio are currently second, behind Sporting, while Cruzeiro of Brazil are favourites for the chop, having lost their all three games so far.

Penarol's win was their second in two games in group five and suggested that the club, once a power in international soccer, could be coming out of the doldrums. Last week they thrashed local rivals Nacional 4-1.
Cerro Porteno's defeat was their third in three games, leaving them firm favourites to be knocked out of a group which also includes Oriente Petrolero of Bolivia and Guarani of Paraguay.
Bolivar top group one, having won all three games and scored eleven goals in the process.
